content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes the first system for semi-supervised instance segmentation. It employs the mean teacher system and supervises the student network with pseudo-labeling.

It employs CenterMask2. The experiments are conducted on the COCO dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
++The paper shows  the possibility of doing semi-supervised learning with CenterMask2. 
++The performance has been improved by using unlabeled data.
++It is a simple framework.

--The paper directly adopts the Mean Teacher method to the instance segmentation. It would be better if the author could explain the main technique contribution for changing to the new task. Is there any special design that modified the mean teacher or deals with some challenges that are specifically related to instance segmentation or one-stage detector?

-- The comparison experiments are only conducted with a mask-RCNN method, which is not sufficient. Different semi-supervised methods should be applied to the same baseline networks.

--The ablation studies can not well demonstrate the motivation and the effectiveness.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The method is straightforward and easy to follow, however, the experiment parts are not well organized.

Not novel due to its weakness shown in the above question.

The paper could be reproduced because the code is included.
content.summary_of_the_review: I will vote for rejection due to the experiment's organizing. If the author could provide more special designs that they conduct to modify the mean teacher to CenterMask2, it would be better.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a method for semi-supervised instance segmentation, with an anchor-free detector CenterMask. Specifically, the authors adopt the teacher-student mechanism with UnbiasedTeacher for pseudo-label generation. To filter noisy pseudo-labels, the classification and mask IoU scores are used with thresholds. Experiments are conducted on MS COCO.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength**
* The paper is easy to follow
* Semi-supervised instance segmentation is an important task to tackle
* Experiments show promising results

**Weakness**

Technical novelty and motivation
* The main concern of this paper is the technical contribution, as most components in the proposed method are existing, e.g., CenterMask, UnbiasedTeacher, pseudo-label thresholding. This makes this paper look like an engineering pipeline in a technical report.
* The motivation of using the anchor-free detector is not described clearly.

Experiments
* Although achieving promising performance in Table 1, there should be more baseline comparisons. For example, how does teacher-student model works for different methods, e.g., CenterMask, FCOS, CenterNet, or two-stage detectors? For the proposed method, it looks like one of this baseline instead of a newly proposed method to tackle the semi-supervised instance segmentation task.
* There should be more discussions about the limitation and failure cases in the proposed method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The implementations of the proposed method is provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, although the tackled problem setting is important, the technical novelty and contribution are very limited as all the components come from existing methods. Therefore, it would be difficult to provide an acceptance rating.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper addresses the problem of semi-supervised instance segmentation by leveraging the famous mean-teacher framework for semi-supervised learning for image classification. The authors made modifications to Mask-RCNN to make it a student-teacher network. They also arguably claim they are the first to propose semi-supervised instance segmentation. They evaluate the proposed approach on the famous COCO dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
*Strength*
+ The structure of this paper is easy to follow
+ They conduct experiments to verify their method's effectiveness and ablation studies on some important parameters.
 
*Weaknesses*
+ The main methods they use in this paper are not new: the teacher-student framework, the Mask-RCNN architecture, and the mask-scoring technique. The teacher-student framework is already widely used in all kinds of semi-supervised learning including image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection... The Mask-RCNN is very well-known for instance segmentation. And the mask-scoring technique is also widely used to improve the performance of Mask-RCNN. 
+ They claim they are the first to propose semi-supervised instance segmentation. However, there is a research paper titled Noisy Boundaries (Wang et. al., 2022), which is published in CVPR 2022. The authors might work with the problem long ago but the Noisy Boundary paper has already been published so they cannot claim this novelty. 
+ The teacher-student technique is widely used for semi-supervised object detection. Thus, it is trivial to extend an object detector to work with instance segmentation, especially with the Mask-RCNN-based family. If the authors want to have some novelty here, they should propose something which is not trivially extended from Mask-RCNN. 
+ Why did not the authors evaluate their proposed approach on the same validation set of Noisy Boundaries for fair comparison?
+ For the ablation study, they need to include a table showing each component's importance: base, mask thresholding, bounding box thresholding, and a combination of them.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
+ The paper is easy to follow
+ Reproducibility: this paper's experiments can be reproduced.
+ Novelty: This paper lacks novelty as described above in both problem novelty and method novelty.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper basically lacks novelty. Their proposed problem is already introduced in Wang et. al, 2022 and their proposed methods are trivial to adapt from semi-supervised object detection to semi-supervised instance segmentation.

content.title: Polite Teacher: Semi-Supervised Instance Segmentation with Mutual Learning and Pseudo-Label Thresholding
content.TL;DR: We present Polite Teacher, a mutual learning framework with pseudo-label thresholding for single-stage semi-supervised instance segmentation.
content.abstract: We present Polite Teacher, a simple yet effective method for the task of semi-supervised instance segmentation. The proposed architecture relies on the Teacher-Student mutual learning framework. To filter out noisy pseudo-labels, we use confidence thresholding for bounding boxes and mask scoring for masks. The approach has been tested with CenterMask, a single-stage anchor-free detector. Tested on the COCO 2017 val dataset, our architecture significantly (approx. +8 pp. in mask AP) outperforms the baseline at different supervision regimes. To the best of our knowledge, this is one of the first works tackling the problem of semi-supervised instance segmentation and the first one devoted to an anchor-free detector. The code is available.
